title: Graphing a Right-Shifted Two-Thirds Power Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = (x - 8)^(2/3) by identifying its parent function, transformation, cusp location, domain, range, and intercepts.

steps.title: Identify the Parent Function and Horizontal Shift
steps.explanation: Start with the parent curve y = x^(2/3) and replace x with x - 8 to shift the entire graph 8 units to the right.
steps.why: Replacing x with x - 8 translates every point on y = x^(2/3) right by 8 units.

steps.title: Determine the Cusp, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The cusp at the origin moves to (8, 0), the domain is (-infinity, infinity), and the range is [0, infinity).
steps.why: Because (cbrt(x - 8))^2 >= 0 for all real x and vanishes at x = 8, the global minimum is (8, 0).

steps.title: Find the Intercepts and Symmetric Guide Points
steps.explanation: At x = 0, y = (-8)^(2/3) = 4, giving the y-intercept (0, 4). Symmetric points about x = 8 include (7, 1), (9, 1), and (16, 4).
